newsitem.title: CHINA: China stock indices end mostly higher on reversal.
newsitem.headline: China stock indices end mostly higher on reversal.

text.p: China shares ended mostly higher on Wednesday on speculative buying after sharp losses on Tuesday, brokers said.
The Shanghai foreign currency B index edged up 0.007 points, or 0.01 percent, to 73.327 on volume of 18.59 million shares worth $9.1 million.
Brokers said a cautious mood continued to dominate the B share market on concerns about a possible new official crackdown on volatility.
Bargain-hunting late in the session reversed early losses, but overseas investors remained on the sidelines with the 1996 results of most firms still to be released, they said.
Only seven of 43 Shanghai B share listed firms have so far issued their results with the April 30 deadline approaching.
Shanghai Lianhua Fibre was the star performer, jumping $0.012, or 6.06 percent, to $0.210, but on thin volume of 1,000 shares.
China First Pencil was the most traded stock on institutional selling. It ended down $0.002, or 0.42 percent, at $0.464 on volume of 2.5 million shares.
The Shenzhen B share index was dragged down by Chongqing Changan Automobile Co Ltd, which reported a substantial drop in profits for 1996.
The index slid 1.56 points, or 0.98 percent, to 157.77 on turnover of HK$80.16 million from HK$64.57 million on Tuesday.

In its annual report issued on Wednesday, Changan said its post-tax profits for 1996 fell 7.87 percent to 202.83 million yuan compared with 220.16 million in 1995, based on international accounting standards.
Changan was the day's biggest loser, falling HK$0.32, or 7.02 percent, to HK$4.24, after touching an intra-session low of HK$4.10, on volume of 1.05 million shares.
"Changan dived on poor results but the share is unlikely to fall further as it now looks quite cheap," said one analyst.
Shanghai's domestic A share index surged despite Beijing's recent warnings to the market over investment risks. A speculative mood prevailed, brokers said.
The A index put on 42.496 points, or 3.25 percent, to 1,349.527 on turnover of 11.9 billion yuan. The SSE30 index rose 88.118 points, or 2.54 percent, to 3,560.416.
Changan Information was the star on speculative buying, gaining 0.95 yuan, or 10.05 percent, to 10.40 yuan on volume of 4.2 million shares.
The Shenzhen A share index gained 9.29 points, or 2.04 percent, to 465.67. Turnover was 10.3 billion yuan against 11.7 billion yuan the previous session.
